s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with hypotension and rash in a patient with a history of chronic infection and immunomodulatory therapy
salient_findings: widespread, nontender, erythematous patches and thin plaques with telangiectases and hyperpigmentation
history of pembrolizumab treatment with a previous morbilliform reaction
key_facts: patient is a woman in her 50s
history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis
being treated with fluconazole
admitted for fever, hypotension, and rash
pembrolizumab treatment was stopped 3 months prior due to a morbilliform reaction
new skin eruption had been ongoing for 1 to 2 weeks
skin eruption is widespread, asymptomatic, and different from previous reaction
white blood cell count of 4100/μL
absolute neutrophil count of 2940/μL
hemoglobin level of 8.2 g/dL
platelet count of 62 ×103/μL
blood culture results showed no growth at 1 week
serum β-D-glucan, galactomannan, Coccidioides antibody, and immunodiffusion results were negative
respiratory viral panel and SARS-CoV-2 test results were negative

shortlist.label: Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: skin biopsy showing intravascular atypical cells

shortlist.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: widespread, asymptomatic skin eruption with atypical cells on biopsy

shortlist.label: Natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: aggressive lymphoma with skin involvement, consistent with patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: systemic symptoms such as fever and hypotension, along with skin eruption

shortlist.label: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: skin eruption with atypical cells, consistent with lymphoma diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient's skin biopsy findings showing intravascular atypical cells, along with the presence of a widespread, asymptomatic skin eruption and significant laboratory abnormalities such as low platelet count and hemoglobin level, are most consistent with intravascular large B-cell lymphoma.

rejected.label: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The skin biopsy findings and clinical presentation do not strongly support this diagnosis, as cutaneous T-cell lymphoma typically presents with more specific skin lesions and the biopsy would likely show different immunophenotypic markers.

rejected.label: Natural killer/T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy findings do not align well with this diagnosis, which often involves the nasal cavity and would show distinct immunohistochemical features.

rejected.label: Angioimmunoblastic T-cell lymphoma
rejected.why: While this condition can present with rash and fever, the biopsy findings and laboratory results provided do not specifically support this diagnosis, which typically involves systemic lymphadenopathy and distinct histological features.

rejected.label: Anaplastic large cell lymphoma
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and biopsy results do not strongly support this diagnosis, as anaplastic large cell lymphoma often presents with lymphadenopathy and distinct immunohistochemical markers, such as CD30 positivity, which were not mentioned.
